newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Americas trade meeting ends without consensus.
newsitem.headline: Americas trade meeting ends without consensus.

text.p: A three-day meeting in northeast Brazil of commerce ministers from the Americas ended without clear progress toward setting up a regionwide free trade zone, newspapers reported on Friday.

Sebastiao do Rego Barros, general secretary of Brazil's Foreign Ministry, told the news wire Agencia Estado that "substantial differences" between countries debating the Free Trade Area of the Americas (FTAA) had barely begun to be discussed at the meeting.
Deputy commerce ministers from 34 countries in the region began the talks on Tuesday, hoping to make progress toward setting up a free trade zone by the year 2005, as agreed in the 1994 Miami summit.

Trade watchers had predicted a dispute on the pace of tariff cuts between the United States and the South American Mercosur trade bloc, led by Brazil, would dominate the debate in the northeastern tourism resort of Recife.
The United States was pressing for negotiations on tariff cuts to begin after a presidential FTAA summit in Chile in May 1998.

Brazil and its Mercosur partners Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay want to proceed methodically, dealing with bureaucratic barriers to trade and subsidies, in particular for agriculture, before negotiating tariff reductions.
The Brazilian financial daily Gazeta Mercantil said the Recife meeting participants could not even agree on the briefs of 11 working groups set up to study various areas of economic integration.
"Any attempt at conciliation was left to subsequent meetings," it reported.
It said the Americans had been pressing for the working groups to go beyond simply drawing up detailed studies of each country's trade legislation.

"For Mercosur, this is equivalent to advancing the negotiations, which is precisely what we don't want," Jose Botafogo Goncalves, subsecretary for regional and economic integration at the Brazilian Foreign Ministry, told Gazeta.
Brazilian officials were still in Recife and unavailable for comment.

The Recife talks were intended as a preparatory meeting for a ministerial FTAA summit in the Brazilian city of Belo Horizonte, scheduled for May. Another preparatory meeting will take place in Rio de Janeiro in April.
